documents.title: Generative AI Guidelines for Classroom Use
documents.stance_why: The page sets no AI rule itself. It says "BU faculty must proactively guide" use and asks faculty to "State your policy on GenAI use explicitly in the course syllabus", with recommendations only. That hands the decision to instructors, so delegates.
documents.summary: University-level AIDA recommendations telling faculty to set and explain a GenAI policy in the syllabus, verify AI output, design AI-integrated and process-focused assignments, and be cautious about unreliable detectors. Points to the free TerrierGPT platform for equity and data security.

units.why: The opening says "BU faculty must proactively guide appropriate and ethical use in coursework", a duty on instructors to set AI guidance; coded P04 (instructor decides) rather than P09 because it does not yet name the syllabus.
units.anchor: BU faculty must proactively guide appropriate and ethical use in coursework

units.why: "It is therefore important for faculty to review what constitutes allowable versus misuse of GenAI in their course" leaves the allowed/misuse line to each course; P04 fits better than P09 since it concerns deciding, not communicating.
units.anchor: review what constitutes allowable versus misuse of GenAI in their course
units.frag_end: misuse of GenAI in their course

units.why: "State your policy on GenAI use explicitly in the course syllabus" is a syllabus-statement requirement addressed to faculty, so P09.
units.anchor: State your policy on GenAI use explicitly in the course syllabus

units.why: "disclosing how the instructors (faculty and student teachers) will use GenAI for lecture preparation, presentations, grading" asks instructors to tell students about their own AI use, so P47 (not P59, which is about what they may use AI for).
units.anchor: disclosing how the instructors (faculty and student teachers) will use GenAI

units.why: "Take time in the first week of class to explain your policy and its rationale" is about communicating expectations at course start; P09 (state expectations) is the closest type though the channel is oral explanation.
units.anchor: Take time in the first week of class to explain your policy and its rationale
units.frag_start: Take time in the first week

units.why: "Make clear distinctions between acceptable and unacceptable uses" asks instructors to separate allowed from disallowed uses; closest is P05 (categories of use), chosen over P09 because the content is the distinction itself.
units.anchor: Make clear distinctions between acceptable and unacceptable uses

units.why: "They are responsible for verifying the accuracy of any AI-generated content" tells students to check AI output, P31.
units.anchor: responsible for verifying the accuracy of any AI-generated content

units.why: "Submitting GenAI-generated work as their own original work may constitute plagiarism" bans passing off AI output as own work; P19 chosen for the content, with P36 the alternate since the misconduct classification is also stated.
units.anchor: Submitting GenAI-generated work as their own original work may constitute plagiarism

units.why: "Misuse of GenAI can lead to violations of the university's academic conduct policies" classes misuse as an academic-conduct matter, P36.
units.anchor: Misuse of GenAI can lead to violations of the university’s academic conduct policies

units.why: "faculty are encouraged to: Design assignments that integrate GenAI in a way that enhances learning, such as using it for brainstorming, editing, or reflection" recommends AI-integrated assignments; P35 (redesign) fits over P15 because it asks faculty to redesign assignments.
units.anchor: Design assignments that integrate GenAI in a way that enhances learning

units.why: "Emphasize learning goals over performance metrics, which can help reduce misuse" recommends a grading emphasis to reduce misuse, a redesign of assessment (P35).
units.anchor: Emphasize learning goals over performance metrics, which can help reduce misuse

units.why: "Consider process-focused assignments and assessing intermediate milestones" asks for process-based assessment (drafts, reflections), P35; P26 does not fit as it concerns faculty design, not a student transcript duty.
units.anchor: Consider process-focused assignments and assessing intermediate milestones towards a final product
units.frag_end: way of working towards a final product

units.why: "all detection tools are highly fallible, both with respect to false positives and false negatives" says detectors are unreliable and asks caution, P39.
units.anchor: all detection tools are highly fallible

units.why: "Apply enforcement policies uniformly to minimize bias" is an enforcement-fairness instruction; no type covers uniform enforcement, and P64 (right to respond) and P53 (bias harms) do not say this, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Apply enforcement policies uniformly to minimize bias
units.policy: Apply enforcement policies uniformly to minimize bias
units.uncovered_note: Enforce AI-misuse policies uniformly across students to reduce bias, noting digitally savvy students evade detection more and less knowledgeable students are caught more.

units.why: "those students who are digitally savvy are more likely to evade detection" is a factual caveat on unequal detection, part of the bias harm of enforcement; P53 (bias and harms) is the closest.
units.anchor: digitally savvy are more likely to evade detection

units.why: "Focus on teaching students how to ethically and thoughtfully engage with GenAI, rather than only punishing misuse" favors teaching responsible use, i.e. AI use as a skill to teach (P44).
units.anchor: Focus on teaching students how to ethically and thoughtfully engage with GenAI

units.why: "Consider issues of equity, access, and security when promoting GenAI usage" asks instructors to weigh equity of access, P51.

units.why: "a high level of data security, up through confidential data ... not approved for use with restricted use data" states TerrierGPT's data-protection limits, P50 (vetted tools, data protection).

documents.title: CDS Generative AI Assistance (GAIA) Policy
documents.stance_why: The policy describes "an otherwise embracing approach to AI tools" but binds students to credit AI, append the full exchange, and not use AI "during in-class examinations, or assignments, unless explicitly permitted". AI is welcome with disclosure and limits, so permit.
documents.summary: Student-drafted CDS policy that embraces AI tools under transparency rules: credit any use, attach the whole exchange and an explanation, and no AI in exams or assignments unless allowed. Instructors grade declared AI use against a lower baseline, may use detectors, and may impose stricter rules.

units.why: "Students should learn how to use AI text generators ... to enhance rather than damage their developing abilities" states the purpose: learn to use AI to build skill, an AI-use-as-skill rationale (P44) over P41 since it is framed positively.
